impact_summary: Amazon DynamoDB in us-east-1 experienced increased API error rates from 11:48 PM PDT on October 19 to 2:40 AM PDT on October 20, caused by an empty regional DNS record. Global table replicas in other Regions saw prolonged replication lag, and customers were affected by cached DNS expiry until 2:40 AM. Downstream effects lasted much longer: new EC2 launches failed from 2:25 AM to 10:36 AM (with some instances lacking connectivity until 1:50 PM), NLB connection errors occurred from 5:30 AM to 2:09 PM, and services including Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, STS, Amazon Connect, the AWS Management Console, and Redshift were impaired, with the overall event ending at 2:20 PM on October 20.

action_items.action: Add a fix so that a DNS Enactor cannot apply a plan older than the currently active plan, enforcing plan generation ordering atomically at the Route53 transaction level rather than relying on a one-time pre-apply check.

Change the plan clean-up process so it never deletes the currently active plan or any plan that could still be referenced, and add a guard that refuses clean-up when the regional endpoint record would become empty.
Implement automated detection and self-repair for an empty or inconsistent regional DNS record, including an alarm that pages on-call when any endpoint has zero healthy IP addresses.
Write and rehearse a runbook for restoring the DynamoDB regional DNS state and re-enabling DNS Enactors, so manual recovery does not depend on ad hoc operator decisions.
Create a documented operational recovery procedure for DWFM lease re-establishment after a dependency outage, including fleet-scale staged lease recovery and throttling guidance.

Make DWFM lease re-establishment resilient to fleet-scale timeouts by batching work, applying exponential backoff, and ensuring retries make forward progress rather than accumulating queued duplicates.
Reduce EC2 control-plane dependency on DynamoDB in us-east-1 by caching droplet state or adding a fallback path so that a DynamoDB outage does not cause lease expiry across the fleet.
Gate NLB health check admission of new EC2 instances until network configuration propagation is confirmed, so instances are not marked unhealthy and removed from DNS due to propagation lag.
Add rate limiting and circuit breaking to the NLB health check subsystem so that alternating health results cannot overload health checks and trigger cascading automatic AZ failover.
Add alarms on Network Manager propagation backlog and latency so backlog growth is detected and acted on before new instances fail to get connectivity.

Audit services in other Regions (for example Redshift IAM user group resolution and Support Center account metadata) for hard dependencies on us-east-1 and add regional fallbacks or cached credential resolution.
Establish a documented scheduled procedure for restarting Lambda SQS polling subsystems and for prioritizing synchronous invocations during capacity constraints, with automated restart on failure.
Reduce DNS TTLs or add proactive cache invalidation guidance for DynamoDB endpoints so that customer recovery after a DNS fix is not delayed by cached records.
Add customer-facing status communication and per-service dashboards for multi-service events so customers can see which dependent services are impaired and why.
